sub_industry: Fabless 利基型/中小容量存储芯片设计
current_cycle_state: AI server and high-end memory demand are tightening global memory supply; niche memory is being repriced through spillover supply-demand effects, but its demand curve is not identical to HBM or server DRAM.

primary_anchor.reason: Break-even transitions and inventory-cycle accounting make near-term PE unstable; revenue scale, gross-margin recovery, and product/customer validation are more informative in the current memory upcycle.

secondary_anchors.reason: Use cycle-normalized revenue and margin once profitability has restarted but is not yet stable.
Separate mature storage products from strategic investments and early-stage connectivity/compute options.
Useful for checking whether the market is paying for revenue scale, AI spillover, localization, or short-term profit.

weak_or_floor_anchors.reason: Fabless IP and customer certification are not fully reflected in book value; inventory impairment can also distort book value.

disabled_anchors.reason: Not decision-useful when trailing earnings are negative, near zero, or dominated by inventory write-down/reversal.
Loss years and break-even crossings make six-method profit CAGR unstable; use revenue, gross profit, and normalized margins instead.

anchor_switch_rationale: Traditional memory-cycle valuation often leans on PB or trough/peak PE. In the current cycle, AI-driven capacity allocation and memory-price recovery have shifted market focus toward revenue scale, gross-margin repair, supply access, and normalized earnings power. PB remains a floor check rather than the primary language.
valid_when: memory pricing is rising or supply remains tight
gross margin is recovering and inventory impairment pressure is easing
revenue growth reflects real shipment/customer adoption rather than channel stuffing
cash burn is manageable and balance sheet can support R&D through the cycle
invalid_when: memory contract prices roll over for multiple quarters
inventory days or impairment provisions rise faster than revenue
gross margin recovery is mainly from write-down reversal rather than new-product economics
peer-market valuation shifts back to trough PB or cash-burn liquidation logic
large new supply is scheduled to enter and pricing power weakens
key_cycle_indicators: inventory days and inventory impairment ratio
revenue growth split between volume, ASP, and mix
wafer supply and foundry cost trend

sources.name: SIA global semiconductor sales and memory growth data
TrendForce memory contract-price and supply-demand commentary
Company annual and interim reports for target and peers

analyst_notes: Update quarterly or immediately after a memory-price rollover, major AI/server capex revision, peer valuation regime change, or large inventory impairment signal.
